data.note: CSS custom property --data in frontend/src/styles.css; tokens there are named without the colour slug used here (--bg, --plate, --display, --ink-2...).

data-deep.note: Literal in the build (not a custom property): hover of the solid blue key.

data-fill.note: Data Area Fill is #3b82f6 at 10% alpha; ramp shown for the base hue.

gate-fill.note: Gate Wash is #f97316 at 10% alpha; ramp shown for the base hue.

on-data.note: Literal in the build (not a custom property): text on the solid blue key.

readout.purpose: Headline figure of an objective page and the analyst's single-number answers; reduced to clamp(1.75rem, 2.4vw, 2.25rem) on board tiles. Always rendered settled.

headline.purpose: One per page: the page's business question as a title (h1).

title.purpose: Section and tile headings (h2; tiles at 1.125rem).

body.purpose: Sentences; page leads capped at 64ch, trust notes at 72ch.

body-sm.purpose: Keys, figure labels, captions, trust notes, step lists.

figure.purpose: Every number in prose position: changes, facts (1.0625rem, 560), outcome values, axis ticks (10.5px), table cells.

label.purpose: Uppercase instrument labels only: the 'analytics' mark, the popover's 'How this is computed', fact labels.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: The analyst when it slides in as a drawer below 68.75rem.

shadows.name: menu
shadows.purpose: The slash-command menu above the composer.

shadows.name: palette
shadows.purpose: The Ctrl/Cmd K palette, over a rgb(5 9 18 / 0.6) backdrop with a 3px blur.

shadows.name: palette-active-edge
shadows.purpose: The active row in the palette.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing for every CSS transition and keyframe (--ease-out).

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour, background and border changes on keys, rows, links.

motion.name: nudge
motion.purpose: Small transforms: arrow nudges on hover, chevron rotation, popover fade-and-rise (4px).

motion.name: segmented-thumb
motion.purpose: The segmented thumb sliding to the chosen segment (transform only).

motion.name: page-transition
motion.purpose: View transition: old page fades; new page fades in with a 6px rise and 2px blur.

motion.name: nav-indicator
motion.purpose: The active-nav underline sliding between page keys (view transition).

motion.name: drawer
motion.purpose: The analyst drawer on narrow screens (translate).

motion.name: line-draw-in
motion.purpose: Solid lines trace in, only where a chart has animate on: board tiles and the analyst's results.

motion.name: outcome-grow
motion.purpose: Ranked outcome bars scale in from the left.

motion.name: analyst-replay
motion.value: steps 0.35s stagger 0.09s; text clip-path wipe 0.7s; result 0.5s from 4px blur; expo.out (GSAP)
motion.purpose: The signature staged replay: checked, written, approved, rows, then the answer. A stopped step lands with back.out(3) from scale 1.8.

motion.name: skeleton
motion.purpose: Loading shimmer between Plate and Plate Hover.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every animation and transition, and GSAP motion is skipped.

narrative.overview:
The business is read as a board of markets. Each objective (revenue, reservations, customers, marketing) is a market tile that states its figure, its change and its trend; opening it gives the full chart and the ranked outcomes behind it. The owner locked the palette and type on 2026-11-24: navy grounds, Manrope for words, JetBrains Mono for figures only. The world is a dark instrument panel, calm and dense: plates sit on the navy ground, charts sit in recessed wells, and one electric-blue line carries the data.

Colour is evidence, not decoration. Blue means "this is the data"; green and red mean "this change is good or bad news"; orange means "the gate stopped something". Nothing else gets a hue. Statistics (p-values, correlations, model names, the query) are kept out of the default reading and live behind the info popovers and the analyst's "Show the work". Headline figures always render settled, never counted up; motion is spent on one thing, the analyst's staged replay of how it reached an answer.

The app refuses the category default of a sidebar, a row of KPI cards and a grid of unrelated charts. Navigation is a top bar of page keys; the analyst is docked on the right at full height on wide screens.
keyCharacteristics: Navy ground, flat plates with 1px lines, recessed chart wells: depth by tone, not shadow.
One electric-blue data line with a faint area under it; second series in slate, dashed when it is a projection.
Green and red only on changes, coloured by news, not by direction; the arrow gives the direction.
Orange reserved for the gate: rows a quality rule kept out, a model or question stopped.
Manrope for words, JetBrains Mono (tabular) for figures and nothing else.
Market anatomy repeated on every objective page: figure, change, chart well, ranked outcome rows.
Statistics behind popovers and "Show the work"; the default reading stays in plain language.

rules.name: The One Line Rule
rules.body: One electric-blue data line per chart. Every other series is slate; a projection is slate and dashed. In ranked outcomes only the leading row is blue.

rules.name: The News Not Direction Rule
rules.body: Green is good news and red is bad news, on changes only. A cost that falls is green; the arrow, not the colour, says which way it moved. A change under its "small" threshold says "small" in words and is never dramatised.

rules.name: The Gate Owns Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange appears only where the gate acted: rows kept out of a figure, a model that failed its check, a question the analyst stopped. No orange for emphasis, warnings in general, or decoration.

rules.name: The Mono Means Measured Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for figures alone: values, units, periods, axis ticks, commands, the query. Words, questions and explanations are always Manrope.

rules.name: The Settled Headline Rule
rules.body: A headline figure is rendered at its final value. Nothing counts up; a manager reading over a shoulder must never catch a false number.

rules.name: The Recessed Display Rule
rules.body: Charts never sit directly on a plate: they sit in a display well (darker than the ground, 1px line, 10px corners), the way a reading sits in a screen.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the element floats above the page (drawer, popover, menu, palette). Plates and tiles never get one; hover raises a border to Strong Line instead.

dos: Do draw exactly one series in Data Blue per chart, with its faint area; use Slate Series for every comparison and dash it when it is a projection.
Do colour a change by whether it is good news (`good="down"` for costs) and let the arrow carry the direction; say "small" in words below the threshold.
Do reserve orange for the gate: rows left out, a failed check, a stopped question.
Do set every figure in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals and every word in Manrope.
Do put charts in a recessed display well (Display Well, 1px Line, 10px corners) inside a 12px plate.
Do attach a "How this is computed" popover to every headline figure, and keep p-values, correlations, model names and the query behind popovers or "Show the work".
Do render headline readouts settled at their final value.
Do keep the synthetic-data note visible and quiet on every page.
donts: Don't introduce any hue beyond navy neutrals, Data Blue, Slate, the green/red change pair and Gate Orange.
Don't use green or red to mean "up" or "down"; a falling cost is green.
Don't use orange for emphasis, generic warnings or decoration.
Don't count up, tick, or animate a headline figure; draw-in belongs to the board's first load and the analyst's results only.
Don't put shadows on plates or tiles; shadows are for floating layers only.
Don't crop a value axis to make flat synthetic data look dramatic.
Don't show a currency symbol; the source documents none.
Don't put technical words (fact, dimension, SQL) in the default reading; they belong in "Show the work".
